messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we're deprecating long-lived CI service accounts for GitHub Actions runners. New policy requires OIDC token-based auth per workflow. Opt-in starts June 15, enforcement (deny) for legacy tokens on July 31. Full migration doc: https://go/redwood/ci-oidc-migration :rotating_light:

Aj: timeline? any exceptions for 3rd-party integrators?

Maya: Timeline above. Exceptions may be granted for external vendors that cannot support OIDC; those require an Eng-Security review and a compensating-controls plan. Submit requests to #eng-security and tag with "ci-exception".

Sam: Will self-hosted runners break? we have a couple pools that provision infra using org-level SA creds.

Maya: Self-hosted runners will keep a host identity for provisioning, but workload credentials must migrate to per-workflow OIDC flows. We're providing a temporary shim for transition (see doc). We'll also publish a sample workflow and a test harness.

infra-bot: Automated repo scan scheduled: 2024-06-20 09:00 UTC. Output will list repos using legacy secrets and create issues with remediation guidance. Playbook: /playbooks/ci-oidc-checklist.md

Liz: Are we rotating existing secrets automatically? that's going to create a lot of PRs across infra repos.

Maya: Org-level long-lived tokens will be rotated in phases. Repos flagged by the scan will get a remediation PR with a compatibility shim so owners can test. We'll avoid mass-breaking changes; maintainers can request extra time.

Aj: Who owns external comms? need to coordinate with Customer Success and Sales for any customers that integrate with our CI artifacts.

Maya: @Liz will own cross-org comms and coordinate with CS. @Sam will own the shim and test harness. Eng-Security (cc @eng-security) will own policy enforcement and exceptions.

Sam: I'll open repo ci-oidc-shims and post a demo workflow + a runner test image by next week.

Tom: +1. Quick Q: will this affect Dedicated/Private deployment runners? I run a private VPC cluster with on-prem runners.

Maya: Private/Dedicated deployments: policy is configurable. We will provide a migration guide and recommended config for operators. For managed Dedicated clusters we'll assist; for fully private/on-prem installs, operators should follow the guide and engage Support for help.

Liz: I'll draft the announce email, a short FAQ, and a docs landing page. Planning a one-pager for SREs and infra owners.

Aj: Thanks — appreciate the heads-up and the phased approach.

Maya: TL;DR: deprecate long-lived CI service accounts -> move to per-workflow OIDC tokens. Opt-in starts June 15, enforcement July 31. Migration docs, checklist, and scan are live: https://go/redwood/ci-oidc-migration. Ping me or @infra-bot with repo links if you need help.
